messages:
toni_infra: ap-south1 GPU pool A is stuck provisioning for ~9m. noticed local NVMe write_iops shot up and attach queue piling. kernel logs show nvme reset loops + dentry cache pressure. any eyes? :mag:
rachael_sre: seeing attach failures: scheduler reports node state 'io-pending' and attach retries. janitor queue length jumped to ~14k. can we throttle sweeper?
deepak_ops: quick check: janitor job config in ap-south1 is running sweeper v3 every 2m with batch_size=500. that batch_size might be too aggressive for dense tenant workloads.
yuki_eng: recent deploy did change tempfile-sweeper default batch_size from 200 -> 500 to speed cleanup. didn't canary in ap-south1.
toni_infra: tail dmesg from one impacted host:
```
[ 9876.123456] nvme nvme0: controller reset due to keep_alive timeout
[ 9876.123789] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 987654321
[ 9877.001200] overlayfs: unlink failed: -28
[ 9877.112300] writeback_kthread: stuck for 6000ms, kthread blocked
```
rachael_sre: that unlink failed -28 (ENOSPC?) maybe metadata exhaustion or inode cache pressure. ops-bot can you surface SMART counts and running janitor concurrency?
ops-bot: Janitor metrics ap-south1: queue=13982 concurrency=24 rate=0.6/s. SMART summary: reallocated_sectors_count >50 on 5 nodes, >200 on 1 node. Duplicate nvme resets seen on 7 nodes in last 20m.
deepak_ops: mitigation proposal: 1) immediately reduce sweeper batch_size to 100 and add jitter 2) scale janitor horizontally but add per-namespace enqueue-rate caps 3) move new attaches to warmpool-reserve-ap-south1 for 20m 4) cordon & drain top 3 most affected nodes for fsck and possible drive swap
yuki_eng: agree. also push a rollback of sweeper change to canary-free by next deploy. and add overlayfs gc delay to avoid metadata storms.
toni_infra: I've applied batch_size=100 and jitter=enabled. ops-bot: please shift attaches for label "gpu:interactive" to warmpool-reserve-ap-south1, canary 5% first.
ops-bot: Applied: sweeper batch_size=100 by toni_infra at 02:14 UTC. Route update: 5% gpu:interactive -> warmpool-reserve-ap-south1.
rachael_sre: monitoring attach latency and SLOs. if attach latency >400ms for 5m we escalate. also set alert for nvme reset >3 in 10m per host.
deepak_ops: I/O numbers: pre-spike write_iops ~9k -> peak ~110k, avg latency spiked 30ms -> 85ms. after throttling batch size, write_iops fell to ~45k and attach retries down 40%.
yuki_eng: follow ups: - revert sweeper batch_size change in deploy (PR #5099) - add per-namespace soft-rate to janitor enqueues - schedule overnight maintenance for flagged nodes (fsck -f, replace drive if SMART>150) - instrument overlayfs unlink error paths to gather histogram
toni_infra: cost note: routing to warmpool costs approx $850 for 20m of reserve capacity. acceptable vs risking massive attach failures.
rachael_sre: assigning owners: @yuki_eng PR rollback + instrumentation, @deepak_ops schedule drains & replacements, @toni_infra continue monitoring and update on status.
deepak_ops: will open ticket with node list + SMART dumps and ETA for replacements.
ops-bot: Incident summary: ap-south1 ephemeral NVMe metadata storm caused janitor surge -> high write_iops -> nvme resets -> GPU attach holds. Mitigations applied: sweeper throttled, 5% attach routing to warmpool reserve, cordon plan for worst nodes. Owners: deepak_ops, yuki_eng.
toni_infra: keeping thread open for 2 hours. will page if we see new nvme reset bursts. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
